Batch Processing for Multiple Samples

Source: R/multi_scale_ac.R
multiScaleAC_batch.Rd

Runs multiScaleAC over many samples, sequentially or in parallel, with resumable checkpointing.

multiScaleAC_batch(
  data_list,
  sample_ids = NULL,
  h_vec,
  ...,
  perms = 1000,
  seed = 333,
  n_cores = 1,
  checkpoint_dir = NULL,
  coords_cols = c("x", "y"),
  gene1_col = "CD274",
  gene2_col = "PDCD1",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

data_list

List of data frames, each containing coordinates and gene expression. Columns are checked for every sample before any computation starts, so a missing column fails immediately rather than hours in.

sample_ids

Character vector of sample identifiers (optional, auto-generated from names if NULL). Must be unique, since checkpoint files are keyed by them.

h_vec

Numeric vector of bandwidths, in the units of the coordinate columns. See multiScaleAC on choosing these.

...

Additional arguments passed to multiScaleAC, for example kernel, permute or nan_policy.

perms

Integer number of permutations per sample.

seed

Integer base seed. Sample i uses seed + i, so samples are not identically permuted while the batch stays reproducible.

n_cores

Integer cores for parallel processing (default 1 = sequential). Parallelism uses forking and is therefore unavailable on Windows, where this falls back to sequential with a warning.

checkpoint_dir

Character directory for per-sample checkpoint files (default NULL = no checkpointing).

coords_cols

Character vector of two coordinate column names.

gene1_col, gene2_col

Character column names for the two genes. These also become the gene names on each result.

verbose

Logical, report progress.

Value

Named list of kernelcomm_result objects, one per sample. A sample that failed is NULL and is reported by a warning.

Checkpointing

Each sample is written to its own file in checkpoint_dir, named after its sample id. Resuming means skipping the samples whose files already exist, so an interrupted batch continues where it stopped and nothing is recomputed.

Per-sample files replace an earlier design that kept one shared list and one shared file. That design lost every result under parallel processing, because mclapply forks and the worker's assignment into the parent's list was discarded, and all workers raced to write the same path.

Files are removed only when every sample has succeeded, so a batch with failures stays resumable.

Multiple testing across samples and pairs

The manuscript applies its FDR threshold across gene pairs. To reproduce that, collect one p-value per pair from these results – sup_p_value is the natural choice, since it summarises the whole curve – and correct across the collection. Do not use adjust_pvalues for this: it corrects across the bandwidths within one result, which are strongly dependent.

See also

export_mxfda_batch for exporting batch results

Examples

# Split the bundled sample into pseudo-samples by field of view.
data(ccRCCExample)
fovs <- split(ccRCCExample, ccRCCExample$fov)
fovs <- fovs[vapply(fovs, nrow, integer(1)) > 100][1:3]

# Bandwidths in millimetres, matching the coordinate units of this dataset.
results <- multiScaleAC_batch(
  fovs, h_vec = c(0.02, 0.05, 0.1), perms = 99, verbose = FALSE
)
vapply(results, function(r) r@observed[1], numeric(1))
#>          61          62          63 
#> 0.001193851 0.006372473 0.003555446 

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# In parallel, with a resumable checkpoint directory.
results <- multiScaleAC_batch(
  fovs, h_vec = c(0.02, 0.05, 0.1), perms = 999,
  n_cores = 4, checkpoint_dir = tempfile("msac_ckpt_")
)
} # }
